title: Winter Is When Contractors Build the Pipeline
h1: Winter is when you build the pipeline
meta: Slow weeks aren't dead weeks. Use winter to build owned assets — reviews, your Google profile, your site — so spring prints. Here's the plan.
short: Use slow weeks to build the owned assets that make spring busy.
statLabel: pays off what you build in winter

body.answer: Winter is build season. Use the slow weeks on owned assets — reviews, your Google profile, your website — because those are what make the phone ring in spring.
body.html:
Slow weeks feel like dead weeks. They're not. They're the only time all year you can actually work ON the business instead of IN it. The shops that use winter well don't scramble in April. They coast into a full spring.

The move is simple: build owned assets. Reviews, your Google Business Profile, and your website don't expire. Every one you improve now keeps paying every month after. That's different from an ad that stops the second you stop paying. For the bigger picture, read surviving the slow season.

body.h2: Stack reviews while jobs are fresh
body.answer: Go back through this year's happy customers and ask for reviews now. Reviews are the asset that decides the call in spring.
body.html:
You've got a whole year of finished jobs behind you. Those customers still remember you. Text them for a review before they forget. This is the highest-value thing you can do in a slow week.

Why it matters: most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey). A pile of fresh reviews going into spring means more of those searches end in your phone ringing. Use how to get more Google reviews for the exact wording.

body.h2: Fix the profile and the site
body.answer: Finish your Google Business Profile and clean up your website so you're findable and the call button is obvious before the busy months.
body.html:
Spend an afternoon finishing your Google Business Profile — photos, categories, service area, hours. Follow the Google Business Profile checklist for contractors so nothing's half-done.

Then open your website on your phone. Phone number above the fold? Call button obvious? Loads fast? Homeowners start planning projects after the holidays, and when they land on your site you want zero friction between them and the call. Fix it now while you have the time.

body.h2: Plug the leaks before volume hits
body.answer: Set up missed-call text-back and tighten your response time now, so you don't drop leads when spring volume comes in.
body.html:
When spring hits, you'll be on the tools and the phone will ring while your hands are full. If a missed call just goes to voicemail, that lead calls the next guy. Set up missed-call text-back now so every missed call gets an instant text back.

Speed is everything once leads come in: responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). Build the system in winter so it's running when you're slammed. More in speed to lead for contractors.

faq.q: Isn't winter just for cutting costs?
faq.a: Cut what's not working, sure. But the smart move is building free owned assets — reviews, profile, site — that cost time instead of money and pay off all spring.

faq.q: What's the single best winter task?
faq.a: Stacking reviews from this year's customers. They still remember you, and reviews decide who gets the call in spring.

faq.q: When will I see the payoff?
faq.a: Spring. Owned assets compound — the profile and reviews you build now keep bringing jobs long after the work is done.
